why: A request written `${base}/v1/…` is only a call on THIS API when `base` holds
this API's origin. PayPal versions its REST API under /v1/ too, and it has a
/v1/billing/subscriptions of its own — so reading the path alone imported six
of PayPal's endpoints into this system's inventory as callers of routes that
do not exist here. The analyzer therefore recognises only the two canonical
base expressions on sight, and every other origin is answered ONCE, here, by
a human who read the binding.
OURS     — the binding resolves to this API's origin; the call is a consumer.
EXTERNAL — a third party's origin; not a route of ours at all.
PLUMBING — our own client wrapper, whose path is supplied by its callers and
is therefore already counted at those call sites.
